material_definitions: In the search for optimized ionic conductors, the lithium argyrodites have attracted a lot of interest.

Here, we systematically explore the influence of aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I using a combination of X-ray and neutron diffraction, as well as impedance spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance.
With increasing Ge content, an anion site disorder is induced and the activation barrier for ionic motion drops significantly.
warnings: Temperature assumed to be room temperature (25 Celsius) as it was not explicitly stated in the source text.
The exact value of x in the formula is not specified, this value corresponds to the 'fastest' composition.

material_definitions: The class of argyrodites Li6PS5X (X = Cl, Br, I) has attracted considerable interest.
If iodine is the halide in the structure (Li6PS5I), no site-disorder occurs due to the large size mismatch between S2– and I–.
warnings: Temperature is inferred as 25 Celsius (Room Temperature).
Data is cited from external work (Kraft et al.).

material_definitions: We have investigated the effect of Ge4+ substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I on the structure transport relationships.
With increasing Ge-fraction, the diffusion pathways for Li+ expand and site disorder between the S2– and I– positions appears.
The increasing disorder is correlated to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in the conductivity.
warnings: Temperature is inferred as 25 Celsius (Room Temperature).
Exact stoichiometry 'x' for the peak conductivity material is not specified in the extracted text.
Uncertainty (± 0.8) is omitted.

material_definitions: Aliovalent substitution was performed in the argyrodite Li6+xP1-xGexS5I to investigate changes to structure and transport.
The substitution induces structural changes, increasing lattice volume, and I-/S2- site disorder.
These changes open up bottlenecks, facilitating inter-cage jumps and dropping the activation barrier.
The argyrodite structure features interpenetration of face-centered cubic lattices.
warnings: Measurement temperature (25 Celsius) is assumed as room temperature, not explicitly stated.

Figure 6: Activation barrier and ionic conductivity of  $Li_{6+x}P_{1-x}Ge_xS_5I$  as a function of the refined Ge content, as obtained from impedance spectroscopy. With increasing  $Ge^{4+}$  and  $Li^+$  concentration, the ionic conductivity increases over three orders of magnitude, reaching a conductivity of  $\sigma = 5.4$  mS cm<sup>-1</sup>. An inflection point starting  $\sim 20\%$  Ge can be seen that leads to a strong decrease of the activation barrier.
